data.title: User Account Control Bypassable
data.summary:
Elevation to full administrative rights was achieved without a consent prompt, using
auto-elevating system components, from an account that was a member of the local
administrators group.
data.description:
User Account Control is a convenience boundary rather than a security one, a position the
vendor states explicitly. Where a user is already an administrator, numerous auto-elevating
components can be induced to run attacker-chosen code at full privilege without a prompt.

The practical consequence is that any treatment of UAC as a control is misplaced: the
protection it appears to offer does not survive an account that holds administrative
membership in the first place.

The real finding is therefore usually the standing administrative rights that make the
bypass available, rather than the bypass technique itself.
data.recommendation:
* Remove standing local administrator membership from user accounts, which eliminates the
  precondition rather than the technique.
* Where administrative rights are required, provide them through a separate account or a
  just-in-time elevation mechanism with its own audit trail.
* Set UAC to always prompt as a defence in depth measure, while recognising it is not a
  security boundary.
data.short_recommendation: Remove standing local administrator rights; UAC is not a security boundary.
